content: Certainly. The benefits of using the medication outweigh the risks. However, when hormonal contraceptives are co-administered, they may not provide reliable birth control. Concurrent use can increase the likelihood of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. Close monitoring is advised. 1. LUMEFANTRINE: This drug reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 2. FERROUS FUMARATE: This compound decreases manganese levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but caution and monitoring are advised. 3. MAVACAMTEN: This drug significantly reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. Both progestin and ethinyl estradiol are substrates of CYP3A4, and mavacamten may decrease their systemic exposure, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Patients should be advised to use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction (e.g., intrauterine systems) or add non-hormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) during co-administration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 4. ETHINYL ESTRADIOL AND METFORMIN: Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. FERROUS FUMARATE AND METHYLDOPA: Ferrous fumarate reduces methylopa levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. METRONIDAZOLE: This drug decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 7. ETHINYL ESTRADIOL AND METYRAPONE: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effects of metyrapone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. Subtherapeutic responses to metyrapone may occur in patients on estrogen-containing therapies, including oral contraceptives. Discontinuation of estrogens prior to and during metyrapone administration may be advisable. 8. ETHINYL ESTRADIOL AND MEXILETINE: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 9. ETHINYL ESTRADIOL AND MIDAZOLAM: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines undergoing oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations and prolonged sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 10. MIFEPRISTONE: This drug decreases the effects of ferrous fumarate and ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Additionally, mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. MINERAL OIL: This substance decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 12. MINOCYCLINE: This antibiotic reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 13. MITOTANE: This drug decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4, and dosage adjustments may be necessary when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 14. MOMELTINIB: This drug increases the toxicity of ethinyl estradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. Momeltinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Dosage adjustments of other BCRP substrates may be necessary. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 15. MOXIFLOXACIN: This antibiotic decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 16. OMBIVIR/ PARITAPREVIR/ RITONAVIR & DASABUVIR: Co-administration with ethinyl estradiol is contraindicated due to significant interaction risks, including ALT elevations observed in clinical trials. Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating this hepatitis C combination regimen and restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 17. OMEPRAZOLE: This drug decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. OXCARBAZEPINE: This drug decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and non-hormonal contraception is advised. 19. PENTOBARBITAL, PHENOBARBITAL, AND PHENYTOIN: These drugs decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 20. PIOGLITAZONE: This drug decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. POSACONAZOLE: This drug increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 22. PRIMIDONE: This drug decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 23. QUINIDINE: This drug increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. QUINUPRISTIN/DALFOPRISTIN: This combination increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised.
